capability_investigated: generate() batched per-item prompt-list decode over multiple feature windows, and how window boundaries map back to text seams
what_i_learned: the fixed-30s mel extractor forces any long-form fix to slice audio, and a hard non-overlapping cut leaves each 30s seam decoded by only one window — so boundary words are both deleted and (across neighbours) duplicated; overlapping the windows makes each seam fully interior to a neighbour, which is recoverable by string-overlap stitching since the shared span is re-emitted identically
hypothesis: cut overlapping 30s windows (25s hop), decode all in one batched generate() call, and stitch adjacent texts by removing the longest duplicated char-run at the seam, to eliminate boundary deletions/duplications that plain chunking left

capability_investigated: generate() sequences_ids contents when the prompt omits <|notimestamps|>, and the relation of timestamp token ids to the <|0.00|> base id
what_i_learned: dropping <|notimestamps|> makes the decode interleave timestamp tokens (ids >= convert_tokens_to_ids("<|0.00|>")) into sequences_ids at 0.02s resolution; the last such token is a model-chosen segment boundary the stub and the prior seam-stitch attempts were throwing away, which lets the window advance to a real boundary instead of a blind 30s cut
hypothesis: replace the single fixed-window decode with a sequential loop that re-enables timestamps and seeks to the last emitted timestamp each window, eliminating tail deletion past 30s and removing fixed-grid seams entirely (no stitching/dedup needed)

capability_investigated: generate() per-item prompt list — token prefix beyond the fixed [sot,lang,task], specifically <|startofprev|> previous-text conditioning
what_i_learned: the prompt list passed to generate() is arbitrary, so the canonical Whisper prev-text context (<|startofprev|> + prior committed text ids, capped near 224) can be prepended; the prior sequential loop decoded every window context-free, which is consistent with the uniform length_ratio<1.0 deletion signal
hypothesis: prepend the running committed transcript (last 224 ids) after <|startofprev|> to each window's prompt so the decoder has continuation context across seams, recovering deleted/under-emitted speech and lowering corpus_cer

capability_investigated: generate() result object fields beyond sequences_ids, specifically the per-sequence confidence score returned when return_scores=True
what_i_learned: the decode result exposes a per-sequence score (avg log-prob) alongside sequences_ids that the loop was discarding; this score is the signal canonical Whisper uses to detect a degenerate window and trigger temperature fallback
hypothesis: greedy decode (beam_size=1, temp=0) occasionally collapses on hard spans producing the uniform length_ratio<1.0 deletion signal, so score-gate each window and re-decode once at sampling_temperature=0.4 when score < -1.0, recovering dropped text without paying compute on confident windows

capability_investigated: generate() beam-search arguments — beam_size, patience, length_penalty — which gate whether decoding is greedy (single hypothesis) or an actual search over multiple hypotheses
what_i_learned: every prior iteration decoded with beam_size=1 (pure greedy); length_penalty is a decode lever that only takes effect under beam search (beam_size>1) and biases the search toward longer hypotheses, so the uniform length_ratio<1 deletion signal has never been attacked with a recall-oriented decoder — greedy Whisper systematically under-generates dense Korean speech
hypothesis: replace greedy beam_size=1 with beam_size=3 + length_penalty=1.0 so the decoder explores higher-recall completions and resolves ties toward longer transcripts, directly countering the uniform deletion; beam kept narrow to respect the 152.3s runtime budget

capability_investigated: generate() num_hypotheses argument and the per-item results[0].sequences_ids list — whether beam search can return more than the single top-scored hypothesis the loop has always taken
what_i_learned: with beam_size>1 the decoder already explores N hypotheses internally; num_hypotheses=N makes results[0].sequences_ids return all N (not just [0]), exposing lower-ranked-but-longer beam members that the top-1 selection was discarding
hypothesis: request num_hypotheses=3 and select the hypothesis with the most decoded text tokens per window, because the uniform length_ratio<1 / near-zero-hallucination diagnosis means recall is the bottleneck and the top-scored beam is systematically the shortest-safe transcription

capability_investigated: generate() beam-search length_penalty magnitude — its scoring direction (score = logprob_sum / pow(len, lp)) and whether raising it above the neutral 1.0 every kept run has used actually shifts the top beam toward longer hypotheses
what_i_learned: in the ctranslate2-style decode the length normalization divides a negative cumulative log-prob by pow(length, length_penalty), so lp>1.0 makes longer sequences score relatively higher; the ledger noted this lever exists but it was never set off-neutral, leaving the uniform length_ratio<1 deletion signal unattacked by an actual length reward (only by introducing beam at lp=1.0)
hypothesis: raise length_penalty 1.0 -> 1.5 (sole change) so beam search prefers longer hypotheses and recovers the dropped tail syllables driving the uniform sub-1.0 length_ratio, especially on the worst-CER 0.87-0.92-ratio files

capability_investigated: generate() decode-time token gating — the suppress_blank flag and the default suppress_tokens=[-1] non-speech suppression set, never set in any prior iteration
what_i_learned: the ledger-confirmed kwarg passthrough (return_scores, num_hypotheses both took effect) means generate() forwards ctranslate2 Whisper decode kwargs, so suppress_blank/suppress_tokens are reachable; every kept run left them at default (-1 → Whisper's ~90-token non-speech set + blank-suppressed first token), so the decoder has always been forbidden from emitting a whole token class — an unlifted recall constraint orthogonal to beam/length_penalty/num_hypotheses
hypothesis: set suppress_blank=False and suppress_tokens=[] on the existing beam decode so no token is gated out at any step, attacking the uniform length_ratio<1 deletion signal with a recall lever the search-based levers could not touch, at zero added runtime
